sources.entry: NutriTrace - Nutrition and diet tracker with barcode scanning, wearable integrations (Fitbit, Withings, Garmin, Health Connect), adaptive calorie goals, multi-user sharing, and a built-in AI assistant (alternative to MyFitnessPal, Cronometer). (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: NutriTrace is a self-hosted nutrition and calorie tracker that runs as a single Docker container, with a browser PWA and a native Android app.
summary.what_it_does: NutriTrace provides a food diary with configurable meal slots, a personal food/meal/recipe database, and barcode and label scanning via Open Food Facts and an AI OCR feature. It offers calorie goals in Fixed, Dynamic, or Adaptive TDEE modes, plus manual activity logging and an intermittent fasting timer. Optional integrations include Fitbit (via Google Health), Withings, Garmin, and Health Connect, with computed Sleep, Readiness, and Resilience scores. Trace AI can answer questions about your data and propose food entries from photos for you to confirm, and an MCP server and /api/v1 Bearer-token API expose data to external tools. Data is stored in SQLite with uploads on disk, and the app supports multi-user accounts with OIDC SSO. An offline mode in the browser and Android app syncs changes when the connection returns.
use_cases: track daily calories and macros for self-hosting
sync fitness data from Fitbit, Garmin, or Withings
scan food barcodes and labels into a diary
migrate diary data from MyFitnessPal, Lose It, or Cronometer
share a nutrition tracker among household users with SSO
how_to_run: Create a docker-compose.yml using the image ghcr.io/traceapps/nutritrace:latest with port 3001, volumes for DB and uploads, and DB_PATH, UPLOADS_PATH, and JWT_SECRET set.
Generate a JWT secret with: openssl rand -base64 48
Start the container with: docker compose up -d
Open the app in a browser and complete the first-run wizard to create an admin account.
Update later with: docker compose pull && docker compose up -d
notable: No accounts on external services, no telemetry, and data stays on the user's hardware unless a third-party integration is enabled
Offline-first browser and Android app that syncs when reconnected
Local Parquet mirror of Open Food Facts for air-gapped setups
MCP server and scoped Bearer-token API for external AI agents, off by default
caveats: No iOS or iPhone app; the author says building one needs a Mac and developer accounts
Trace AI, Scan Label, and Adaptive TDEE outputs are informational only and not medical advice, per the disclaimer
Built and maintained by a single person, according to the README
